proposals.before: In the first year of Longchang, at the junction of beam and column in the fasting hall of Liu Ziqing, Prince of Luling, blood flowed without cause.
proposals.after: In the first year of Longchang, at the junction of beam and column in the fasting hall of Xiao Ziqing, Prince of Luling, blood flowed without cause.
proposals.reason: Southern Qi imperial princes were of the Xiao house; 廬陵王子卿 is Xiao Ziqing, not Liu Ziqing (Liu is the Song surname).

proposals.before: the second year of Jianyuan, intercalary month, jichou day — rain mixed with snow.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jianyuan, intercalary month, jichou day — rain mixed with snow.
proposals.reason: Sentence-initial English must be capitalized; the idiomatic line currently begins with a lowercase letter.

proposals.before: the first year of Jianyuan, tenth month, renwu night — lightning, then thunder.
proposals.after: In the first year of Jianyuan, tenth month, renwu night — lightning, then thunder.
proposals.reason: Sentence-initial English must be capitalized; the idiomatic line currently begins with a lowercase letter.

proposals.before: the fourth year of Jianyuan, fifth month, new moon of the day wuwu: hail fell.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Jianyuan, fifth month, new moon of the day wuwu: hail fell.
proposals.reason: Sentence incorrectly begins lowercase mid-paragraph style; English needs an initial capital and optional In for a complete sentence.

proposals.before: under Dong Hun they judged it ill that skirts meant to hang below now hung above—ill-omened—and had them cut away.
proposals.after: In Dong Hun’s time they judged it ill-omened that skirts meant to hang below now hung above, and had them cut away.
proposals.reason: Redundant double 'ill'/'ill-omened' and awkward clause order obscure 不祥 as a single judgment.

proposals.before: The west quarters were already ash; the emperor moved to the east quarters—the hall where Emperor Gaozong had lived.
proposals.after: The west quarters having already burned, the emperor moved to the east quarters—the hall where Emperor Gaozong had lived.
proposals.reason: 'Already ash' invents a metaphor not in 既火; Chinese only states the west quarters had already caught fire/burned.

proposals.before: the first year of Jianyuan, eleventh month, gengxu day: at night wind burst up; cloud and thunder shut out the sky; it came from the northwest along the xu-hai quarter.
proposals.after: In the first year of Jianyuan, eleventh month, gengxu day: at night wind burst up; cloud and thunder shut out the sky; it came from the northwest along the xu-hai quarter.
proposals.reason: Sentence must begin with a capital; the idiomatic English incorrectly opens lowercase.

proposals.before: the second year of Jianyuan, summer: in Shiyang, Luling, the Chang stream scoured the mountain foot until six or seven zhang fell away; beneath lay a thousand-odd pillars, each ten arm-spans thick, from one zhang down to eight or nine chi, their heads carved with ancient script no one could read.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jianyuan, summer: in Shiyang, Luling, the Chang stream scoured the mountain foot until six or seven zhang fell away; beneath lay a thousand-odd pillars, each ten arm-spans thick, from one zhang down to eight or nine chi, their heads carved with ancient script no one could read.

proposals.before: Jiang Yan consulted Wang Jian, who said: "South of the Yangtze they no longer read clerical script — these are Qin-Han pillars."
proposals.after: Jiang Yan consulted Wang Jian, who said: "East of the Yangtze they no longer read clerical script — these are Qin-Han pillars."
proposals.reason: 江東 means Jiangdong (east of the Yangtze), not south; the literal field already has East of the River.

proposals.before: the second year of Jianyuan, intercalary sixth month, bingxu: thunder and lightning in the fifth watch of the night.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jianyuan, intercalary sixth month, bingxu: thunder and lightning in the fifth watch of the night.
proposals.reason: Sentence must begin with a capital; the idiomatic English incorrectly opens lowercase.

proposals.before: Yongmin year 3 — great drought; the next year Tang Yu rose in revolt.
proposals.after: Yongming year 3 — great drought; the next year Tang Yu rose in revolt.
proposals.reason: Chinese 永民 is a corruption of the reign name 永明 (Yongming); idiomatic English already has Yongming, but the literal still reads Yongmin.

proposals.before: Crown Prince Wenhuai in the Eastern Palace wrote "Two Ends, Fine and Fine"; its last line was "jade mountains crumble, stone on stone"—after that great princes and chief ministers fell one after another, and both palaces buried their lords.
proposals.after: Crown Prince Wenhui in the Eastern Palace wrote "Two Ends, Fine and Fine"; its last line was "jade mountains crumble, stone on stone"—after that great princes and chief ministers fell one after another, and both palaces buried their lords.
proposals.reason: 文惠 is Wenhui, not Wenhuai; the English romanization misreads 惠 as huai.

proposals.before: Crown Prince Wenhuai in the Eastern Palace composed the poem "Two Ends, Fine and Fine"; the closing line ran "jade mountains topple, heap on heap"—from then on senior princes and chief ministers died in succession, and both palaces saw the emperor die.
proposals.after: Crown Prince Wenhui in the Eastern Palace composed the poem "Two Ends, Fine and Fine"; the closing line ran "jade mountains topple, heap on heap"—from then on senior princes and chief ministers died in succession, and both palaces saw the emperor die.
proposals.reason: 文惠 is Wenhui, not Wenhuai; the literal English repeats the same romanization error.

proposals.before: Wenhuai wrote seven-character verses whose last line always ended "sorrow—and the Harmonious Emperor."
proposals.after: Wenhui wrote seven-character verses whose last line always ended "sorrow—and the Harmonious Emperor."
proposals.reason: 文惠 is Wenhui; idiomatic English incorrectly romanizes the crown prince as Wenhuai.

proposals.before: Crown Prince Wenhuai composed seven-character poems; the closing line always ran "grief and the Emperor of Harmony."
proposals.after: Crown Prince Wenhui composed seven-character poems; the closing line always ran "grief and the Emperor of Harmony."
proposals.reason: 文惠 is Wenhui; literal English incorrectly romanizes the name as Wenhuai.

proposals.before: Crown Prince Wenhuai laid out the Eastern Fields; wits read the name backward and said "after this a frenzied child."
proposals.after: Crown Prince Wenhui laid out the Eastern Fields; wits read the name backward and said "after this a frenzied child."
proposals.reason: 文惠 is Wenhui, not Wenhuai.

proposals.before: Crown Prince Wenhuai built the Eastern Fields; people reversed the name and said "afterward there will surely be a mad child."
proposals.after: Crown Prince Wenhui built the Eastern Fields; people reversed the name and said "afterward there will surely be a mad child."
proposals.reason: 文惠 is Wenhui, not Wenhuai.

proposals.before: While Xiao Yingkou served as chief clerk the pool held its water; when he died, it drained away once more.
proposals.after: While Xiao Yingzhou served as chief clerk the pool held its water; when he died, it drained away once more.
proposals.reason: English spelling Xiao Yingkou contradicts 蕭穎胄/蕭穎冑 (Yingzhou) used for the same man in s0239c; kou is a transliteration error for zhou.

proposals.before: When Xiao Yingkou was chief clerk, the water stopped leaking; when Yingkou died, it leaked dry again.
proposals.after: When Xiao Yingzhou was chief clerk, the water stopped leaking; when Yingzhou died, it leaked dry again.
proposals.reason: Literal English uses Yingkou for 穎胄, but the same person is Xiao Yingzhou (蕭穎冑) in s0239c; standardize to Yingzhou.

proposals.before: the second year of Jianyuan: Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing commanderies were struck by great floods.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jianyuan, Wu, Wuxing, and Yixing commanderies were struck by great floods.
proposals.reason: Sentence begins with a lowercase letter and lacks a preposition, producing ungrammatical English.

proposals.before: the fourth year of Jianyuan, tenth month, bingwu: after sunset, earth-fog rose thick and pulsing like smoke from a fire.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Jianyuan, tenth month, bingwu: after sunset, earth-fog rose thick and pulsing like smoke from a fire.
proposals.reason: Sentence begins with a lowercase letter, producing ungrammatical English.

proposals.before: Yongming 5: in Dongqian, Wuxing, a woman of Wu Xiu's household bore twin boys joined from the chest down and from the navel up.
proposals.after: Yongming 5: in Dongqian, Wuxing, a woman of Wu Xiuzhi's household bore twin boys joined from the chest down and from the navel up.
proposals.reason: Chinese 吳休之 is the full personal name Wu Xiuzhi; English drops the final 之.

proposals.before: Yongming year 5, a woman of Wu Xiu's household in Dongqian, Wuxing, gave birth to twin boys — joined from the chest down and from the navel up.
proposals.after: Yongming year 5, a woman of Wu Xiuzhi's household in Dongqian, Wuxing, gave birth to twin boys — joined from the chest down and from the navel up.
proposals.reason: Chinese 吳休之 is Wu Xiuzhi; literal English should retain the full name.

proposals.before: In Yongming, Prince Zihan of Nanhai governed Southern Xuzhou; a roe deer entered Guangling, leapt into a well, and died; an elephant came to Guangling as well — and later the inspector, Prince Zijing of Anlu, was murdered in his commandery.
proposals.after: In Yongming, Prince Zihan of Nanhai governed Southern Yanzhou; a roe deer entered Guangling, leapt into a well, and died; an elephant came to Guangling as well — and later the inspector, Prince Zijing of Anlu, was murdered in his commandery.
proposals.reason: Chinese 南兗州 is Southern Yanzhou; Xuzhou would be 徐州.

proposals.before: During Yongming, Prince Zihan of Nanhai was Governor of Southern Xuzhou; a roe deer entered Guangling city and threw itself into a well and died; an elephant also came to Guangling — afterward the Inspector, Prince Zijing of Anlu, was killed at his post.
proposals.after: During Yongming, Prince Zihan of Nanhai was Governor of Southern Yanzhou; a roe deer entered Guangling city and threw itself into a well and died; an elephant also came to Guangling — afterward the Inspector, Prince Zijing of Anlu, was killed at his post.
proposals.reason: Chinese 南兗州刺史 is Governor of Southern Yanzhou, not Xuzhou.
